A: The sagittal view shows severe aortic calcification and luminal compromise, correlating with the presentation of chronic mesenteric ischemia described in the caption. B: The coronal view illustrates extensive aortic calcification and narrowing, consistent with the vascular disease context of chronic mesenteric ischemia. C: This panel highlights severe supra-celiac aortic calcification, which is a key indicator of advanced atherosclerotic disease related to the patient's condition. D: This panel shows atherosclerotic narrowing of the distal aorta and iliac arteries, reflecting the systemic vascular burden contributing to chronic mesenteric ischemia.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows pneumoperitoneum, a grave consequence of the underlying acute-on-chronic ischemic process documented in this case of mesenteric ischemia. B: Panel B illustrates diffusely dilated small bowel loops, a major finding associated with bowel ischemia and obstruction resulting from mesenteric vascular disease. C: Panel C shows direct CT evidence of superior mesenteric artery and celiac trunk ostial stenosis, confirming the underlying cause of the mesenteric ischemia. D: Panel D demonstrates the generalized atherosclerotic burden on the major vessels, which is the etiology for the chronic mesenteric ischemia presented.
